tasks.objective: You are the only source of one fact in this run. FIRST, invent a codename: a single lowercase English word of your own choosing, at least five letters, that is NOT any of workforce, gate, term, glossary, usage, codename, lantern, harbour, token, meadow. Nothing in this repository records it and no other worker can discover it by reading files. SECOND, call read_inbox. A peer task is asking you for that codename. When its question is in your inbox, answer it at once with send_message addressed to that peer's task id, with the codename as the message text and nothing else. If the inbox is empty, wait a few seconds using your shell and call read_inbox again; keep doing that until you have answered the peer, for up to two minutes. THIRD, create the file docs/glossary.md and no other file: line 1 exactly "# Glossary", line 2 exactly "Term: <CODENAME>". Then stop.

You must write a codename that only peer task t1 knows. It appears nowhere in this repository, nowhere in this request and nowhere in your own instructions; t1 invents it at run time, so guessing or inventing one is a failure, not an answer. FIRST, call send_message exactly once, with `to` set to t1's task id, asking it to reply with the codename it invented. SECOND — and this is a hard constraint — do NOT call read_inbox at any point in this task, not even once. You do not need to: the coordinator hands peer messages to you directly while you are working, and t1's answer will simply appear in your conversation as a message beginning "[coordinator message". Your only job is to stay busy until it appears. To stay busy, run this in your shell: /bin/zsh -lc 'sleep 10' , and repeat that same command up to twelve times, checking after each one whether such a message has appeared. THIRD, the moment the codename appears, stop waiting and create the file docs/usage.md and no other file: line 1 exactly "# Usage", line 2 exactly "Uses term: <CODENAME>", using the codename verbatim as it was handed to you. Only if all twelve waits pass with nothing handed to you, write "Uses term: unanswered" and say plainly that nothing was ever handed to you.
